_comment: The ascension site (plan-ascension.md §4.1, built in §12.4 C2a step 1). An INTERACTION-CARRYING MOB, not a prop, and that is a load-bearing choice rather than a convenience: api/props/ definitions parse with DisallowUnknownFields, carry no sensor, and InteractionSystem registers only MobEntitys, so 'an object that talks' has exactly one supported shape and this is it. Copied knob-for-knob from forest-sign.json: role creature + speed 0 (an NPC is an actor that authors no movement), faction townsfolk so player damage skips it, collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) and deliberately NOT Action(2) so no aura on either side can target it, mask 16 = Border only so nothing pushes it, xpFactor 0 to keep it off the nameplate path, aggroRadius 1.0 required-but-inert (interaction.range 2.0 is the wider of the two and is what sizes the one sensor, D7). All values [PLACEHOLDER]. ⚑ entityType Signpost is a DELIBERATE REUSE (§12.3 P12): a stone of its own is a new wire EntityType plus client art, and D20 already deferred the ceremony's art to the world pass, so the site ships wearing the sign's sprite. ⚑ TWO GREETINGS, and the ORDER IS THE FEATURE (L3): the gated one first, the unconditional preview last, because selectNode speaks the first node whose conditions pass and an unconditional node makes every conditional node below it unreachable. minLevel 30 is P1, the whole entry price, and it MUST equal game.player.levelCurve.maxLevel — pinned by TestAscensionSite_ReadyNodeIsGatedAtTheConfiguredMaxLevel, because the duplication is real and a cap change would otherwise leave the stone either unreachable or lying to a player it will refuse. ⚑ THE `catalog` NODE AUTHORS NO OPTIONS AND CANNOT: its rows are GENERATED per player from the ascension catalog (§4.2's first dynamic row source, C2a step 2), and the loader REFUSES authored options on a `rows` node because the two would share one index space. ⭐ IT DOES AUTHOR `rewards`, AND MUST (plan-ascension-sites.md C3 / D5): a site owns the list it offers exactly as C1 made it own its price, there is no catch-all, and an absent list is a boot failure. THE ORDER IS THE INDEX SPACE and it is authored here: the five ungated rewards first, so a player who can take something meets it before the three walls, then Blight, FrostShield and Lantern. ⛑ THAT ORDER IS ALSO A TEST: `Catalog.All()` is sorted by unlock key, so a list left in alphabetical order would serve every row at the index the CATALOG would have given it, and the one bug this feature can have - apply resolving a click against the catalog instead of against this node - would be invisible at every single row. Reordered, it hands over the wrong reward, which is what `c2a-ascension-site.mjs` and TestAscensionSites_AtLeastOneOrdersItsRewardsItself exist to notice (P8). Its `lines` are load-bearing rather than flavour: a generated list may legitimately come back empty (D14), and then the lines are all the node has to say. ⚑ Node ORDER is still L3's rule: the gated greeting first, the unconditional preview LAST; `catalog` sits between them and is reached from BOTH the row above it and (since C2) the `lockedWhenGated` row below it, never as a greeting. ⭐ THAT SECOND ROW IS WHAT MAKES THE PRICE READABLE (plan-ascension-sites.md C2): below the cap the preview now shows 'Show me the rewards. - locked: level 30 (12/30)' rather than nothing, the number composed live from `catalog`'s own conditions. The preview's lines therefore do NOT name the price any more — a hand-typed 'Needs a max-level character' beside a gate is the same duplication C1 took out of Go, and it goes stale the same way. ⚑ TEXT is plain and [PLACEHOLDER] (the TownCrier convention): §8 still owes the site a lore write, 'The Passing' being the candidate framing, and D4 fixed the tone as ASCENSION, positive — a life laid down, never a sacrifice extracted. ⭐ THE `catalog` NODE CARRIES THE CAP GATE TOO, and it is not redundant with `ready`'s: present() makes the FIRST node whose conditions pass the greeting, so an ungated catalog node became the level-1 greeting (a fresh character was shown the reward list), and applyGrant validates a row against its NODE's conditions, so an ungated one also let a crafted message stash a pick below the cap. Caught by c2a-ascension-site.mjs at C2a step 3. The rule to carry: a node that is not meant to be a greeting must be gated so it cannot be selected as one; L3's loader check does NOT cover this, because it only refuses a conditional node sitting BELOW an unconditional one.
